formula_checks.name: buildPerformance
formula_checks.why: Most of the row is assembled right from the functions it names, and measuring the yardstick over the same dates as the holding is right. Three faults. (1) A holding bought inside the period gets its return on cost (MK-PF-F-007) as its period return. With more than one purchase at different prices that is not a time-weighted return (owner decision Q16), and it is set beside a yardstick measured as a pure price return since the first purchase, so 'beat by' compares two different kinds of figure. (2) 'Bought AFTER the period's start' leaves a purchase made ON the first day uncapped; owner decision Q3 puts the first day inside the period, so money that arrived that day arrived inside it. (3) In a 2Y window uncapped holdings carry a yearly rate (MK-PF-F-010) and capped ones a total (MK-PF-F-007 / MK-PF-F-011), so one column mixes two units, and portfolio and category averages built on these rows (MK-PF-F-019, MK-NW-F-084) mix them too. It also inherits a $0 market value for a holding with no price (MK-PF-F-004).
formula_checks.should_be: Capped when the earliest purchase is on or after the period's first day. A capped holding's period return = its time-weighted return since the first purchase (price-based: chain-linked at each purchase), set against the yardstick since the same day. Within one window, every row's return is in the same unit (all totals, or all yearly rates when the window is over a year).
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decisions Q16 (time-weighted) and Q3 (both edge days inside the period); agreement between rows in one column.

formula_checks.name: benchmarkTicker
formula_checks.why: The mapping for the kinds it names is sensible (SPY for stocks, AGG for bonds, GLD for commodities, AOR for a balanced 529). Two faults. (1) It reads only `kind`, while the app's own Position type says the explicit `asset_class` (set by import or sync) wins over kind: a bond fund the import marks as class 'bond' with no kind is compared against SPY. (2) 'Anything else or none → SPY' invents a yardstick for a holding nothing describes, and for a cash-class holding; the brief's rule is that an honest 'no answer' beats a default (the type comments also record the owner's Q11 'refuse the line and ask' — author-recorded). Low: the registry tags (purchase price and date, account wrapper) do not fit a function that reads only the kind.
formula_checks.should_be: Read the holding's asset class first (it wins over kind), then kind. Stocks/funds → SPY; bonds, fixed income and annuities → AGG; private equity → PSP; hedge funds → QAI; commodities → GLD; crypto → BTC; 529 → AOR. Cash, or nothing that says what the holding is → no yardstick (the comparison is not shown).
formula_checks.rests_on: The app's Position type ('explicit class … wins over kind'); brief: no default number where the honest answer is 'no answer'.

formula_checks.name: topHoldingConcentration
formula_checks.why: Largest holding ÷ total, reported at 25% or more with two or more holdings, is the right fact. The formula does not say whether the 25% line is tested before or after rounding to a whole percent; as worded ('rounded … — reported only when that share is 25% or more') it tests the rounded figure, so a 24.6% holding is reported as 25%. Owner decision Q56 is to round once, at display, so the line should be tested on the full-precision share. It also does not say which holding is named when two are equally largest.
formula_checks.should_be: Share = largest value ÷ total at full precision; report when that share is 25% or more; round to a whole percent only for display. On a tie, name a stated one (for example, the first in the list).
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decision Q56 (round once, at display); brief: a line on the wrong side.

formula_checks.name: attribution
formula_checks.why: A contribution should be the holding's weight at the START of the period × its return, so that the contributions add up to the portfolio's return. The formula weights by value today, which already includes each holding's gain, so winners are over-weighted and the contributions do not add up to the portfolio return. It also divides by the total of ALL holdings, including those with no period return, so the weights of the holdings it lists do not sum to 1 and the contributions cannot add up to MK-PF-F-019's figure either. Parts that do not add up to the whole they sit beside.
formula_checks.should_be: Over the holdings with a period return and value above zero: start value = value now ÷ (1 + return); weight = start value ÷ the sum of those start values; contribution = weight × return. The contributions then sum to the portfolio return (Σ value now ÷ Σ start value − 1).
formula_checks.rests_on: Standard return attribution (beginning-of-period weights); ordinary arithmetic.

formula_checks.name: allocation
formula_checks.why: Value by kind plus cash, share = value ÷ total, largest first, is right. Two gaps. (1) Each share is rounded to one decimal on its own, so the slices shown can add to 99.9% or 100.1% beside a total of 100% — parts that do not add up to the whole. (2) It groups by `kind`, while the Position type says the explicit asset class wins over kind; a holding the import classes as 'bond' with kind 'mutual fund' lands with the funds. Owner decision Q2 also says a position clearly named money market is a fund, not cash; the card does not say how such a holding is grouped.
formula_checks.should_be: Group by the holding's class (class wins over kind; a money-market fund is a fund per Q2), plus cash above zero. Share = value ÷ total at full precision; for display, round to one decimal so the shown shares sum to exactly 100.0 (largest-remainder rounding).
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decisions Q2 and Q56; the Position type comment; ordinary arithmetic.

formula_checks.name: portfolioTrend
formula_checks.why: The question is how the portfolio moved. The formula prices TODAY'S share count at every past date, so it draws what today's holdings would have done, not what the portfolio was. A holding bought halfway through the period appears to have been owned from the start (its money shows up as if it were always there and its price moves before the purchase show as the person's gain or loss); a holding sold during the period vanishes from the past entirely. A holding with no price counts as zero, so the line drops or jumps with no money moving, and with no prices at all it draws a flat line at $0 rather than nothing. It also disagrees with MK-NW-O-008, which reads the actual value of the accounts from the daily record.
formula_checks.should_be: Value at each date = the measured accounts' recorded value on or before that date (the daily record MK-NW-O-008 reads), or failing that, the shares actually held on that date (from purchase and sale dates) × the close on or before it. No point where a holding held on that date has no price. Yardstick line scaled from the first point.
formula_checks.rests_on: Agreement with MK-NW-O-008 (values read from the daily record); brief: missing is not zero.

formula_checks.name: portfolioPeriodReturn
formula_checks.why: Averaging holdings' returns weighted by market value TODAY does not give the portfolio's return: today's value already contains each holding's gain, so winners count for more than they did. The right weights are the values at the start, which is exactly what MK-NW-F-084 (each category's return) does — value at start = value now ÷ (1 + return), return = Σ now ÷ Σ start − 1. The two cards disagree for the same holdings; this card is the wrong one. In a 2Y window it also averages yearly rates with capped holdings' totals (see MK-PF-F-014). The author's renaming of this figure to 'value-weighted' (DEC-0323) does not make it a return of the portfolio.
formula_checks.should_be: Over the holdings with a period return above −100% and value above zero: start value = value now ÷ (1 + return); return = Σ value now ÷ Σ start value − 1 (the same rule as MK-NW-F-084). Nothing when none qualifies.
formula_checks.rests_on: Ordinary arithmetic (a portfolio with no money moved returns Σ end ÷ Σ start − 1); agreement with MK-NW-F-084.

formula_checks.name: portfolioBenchReturn
formula_checks.why: 'The market, matched to my mix' should weight each yardstick by how much of the portfolio that holding was at the START — the mix the market is being compared against. Weighting by value today lets the person's own gains change the market figure (a holding that doubled doubles its yardstick's weight). It also averages over a different set of holdings from MK-PF-F-019: a holding with a yardstick return but no return of its own is in this average and not in that one, so the two figures shown side by side on /home (MK-PF-M-008 beside the person's return) are not about the same money.
formula_checks.should_be: Over the holdings that have BOTH their own period return and a yardstick return, with value above zero: start value = value now ÷ (1 + own return); market = Σ (start value × yardstick return) ÷ Σ start value.
formula_checks.rests_on: Standard benchmark blending (beginning-of-period weights); agreement with the set used by MK-PF-F-019.

formula_checks.name: periodDollarDelta
formula_checks.why: total × r ÷ (1 + r) is the dollar gain only when no money moved during the period. With a time-weighted return (owner decision Q16) and money added or taken out inside the period, today's total includes the money added, so this formula applies the return to money that was not there for the whole period and the dollars no longer equal what the money made. The Home hero then says 'up $X' with an X that disagrees with 'Wealth generated' (MK-PF-M-002) for the same window. It is consistent with MK-NW-F-091 / MK-NW-F-127, which use the same expression for a holding with no flows. Smaller: '0 when an input is not a number or the return is −100% or worse' invents a $0 where there is no answer.
formula_checks.should_be: Dollars shown beside the return = wealth generated over the same window from the walk: ending − beginning − contributions + withdrawals (MK-NW-O-008). total × r ÷ (1 + r) only when nothing moved in or out. No answer (not $0) when an input is missing or the return is −100% or worse.
formula_checks.rests_on: Ordinary arithmetic; agreement with MK-PF-M-002 (wealth generated) via MK-NW-O-008; brief: missing is not zero.

formula_checks.name: categoryEarnings
formula_checks.why: The return rule is right — value at start = value now ÷ (1 + return), category return = Σ now ÷ Σ start − 1 — and it is the rule MK-PF-F-019 should use. The filing of records has two faults. (1) Interest with no ticker goes to 'Cash in this account', but the interest from a CD or bond held as its own account usually arrives with no ticker; it then lands in Cash, and Bonds & CDs (which earned it) is dropped because it 'earned nothing' — while the author's own rule for this table says interest comes from a bond. (2) It files a holding of class 'cash' under Cash, but the app's type comment says that class includes money-market funds, and owner decision Q2 says a position clearly named money market is never counted as cash. Also: in a 2Y window the rows' period returns are yearly rates (MK-PF-F-010), so value now ÷ (1 + yearly rate) is not the value at the start; the category return is then neither a total nor a correct yearly rate.
formula_checks.should_be: Interest on a bond or CD account (or naming a bond) → Bonds & CDs, whether or not it names a ticker; interest with no ticker on a cash account → Cash. A money-market fund (by name, flag or the person's answer) → Stocks / Funds, not Cash (Q2). Use each holding's TOTAL return over the window for the start value; turn the category's total into a yearly rate afterwards when the window is over a year.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decision Q2; the author rule on MK-PF-M-007 ('interest from a bond'); ordinary arithmetic.
